+"""Limit policy model and pure decision logic."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations

+from typing import Literal
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator
+
+
+class RateLimit(BaseModel):

+    per_seconds: float = Field(gt=0)
+
+    @field_validator("per_seconds")
+    @classmethod
+    def _finite_per_seconds(cls, v: float) -> float:
+        if not math.isfinite(v):
+            raise ValueError("per_seconds must be finite")
+        return v
+
+
+class Quota(BaseModel):
+    max_calls: int = Field(gt=0)
+
+
+class LimitPolicy(BaseModel):
+    rate_limit: RateLimit | None = None
+    quota: Quota | None = None
+    scope: Literal["server", "session"] = "server"
+
+
+class LimitDecision(BaseModel):
+    allowed: bool
+    retry_after: float | None = None
+    remaining: int | None = None
+    reason: Literal["rate_limit", "quota"] | None = None
+
+
+def _validate_time_inputs(call_times: list[float], now: float) -> None:
+    if not isinstance(now, (int, float)):
+        raise ValueError("now must be a number")
+    # bool is subclass of int; treat as number is fine
+    now_f = float(now)
+    if not math.isfinite(now_f):
+        raise ValueError("now must be finite")
+    if now_f < 0:
+        raise ValueError("now must be >= 0")
+    for t in call_times:
+        if not isinstance(t, (int, float)):
+            raise ValueError("call_times entries must be numbers")
+        tf = float(t)
+        if not math.isfinite(tf):
+            raise ValueError("call_times entries must be finite")
+        if tf > now_f:
+            raise ValueError("call_times entries must not be after now")
+
+
+def evaluate(policy: LimitPolicy, call_times: list[float], now: float) -> LimitDecision:
+    _validate_time_inputs(call_times, now)
+    now_f = float(now)
+
+    in_window: list[float] | None = None
+    in_window_count: int | None = None
+    if policy.rate_limit is not None:
+        per = float(policy.rate_limit.per_seconds)
+        in_window = [float(t) for t in call_times if now_f - float(t) < per]
+        in_window_count = len(in_window)
+
+    used = len(call_times)
+
+    rate_denies = False
+    if policy.rate_limit is not None:
+        assert in_window_count is not None
+        if in_window_count >= policy.rate_limit.max_calls:
+            rate_denies = True
+
+    quota_denies = False
+    if policy.quota is not None:
+        if used >= policy.quota.max_calls:
+            quota_denies = True
+
+    if quota_denies:
+        return LimitDecision(allowed=False, retry_after=None, remaining=0, reason="quota")
+
+    if rate_denies:
+        assert in_window is not None
+        assert in_window_count is not None
+        assert policy.rate_limit is not None
+        sorted_w = sorted(float(t) for t in in_window)
+        idx = in_window_count - policy.rate_limit.max_calls
+        blocking = sorted_w[idx]
+        retry_after = blocking + float(policy.rate_limit.per_seconds) - now_f
+        return LimitDecision(
+            allowed=False, retry_after=retry_after, remaining=0, reason="rate_limit"
+        )
+
+    # allowed
+    if policy.rate_limit is None and policy.quota is None:
+        return LimitDecision(allowed=True, retry_after=None, remaining=None, reason=None)

+        remainings.append(policy.rate_limit.max_calls - in_window_count - 1)
+    if policy.quota is not None:
+        remainings.append(policy.quota.max_calls - used - 1)
+    remaining = min(remainings)
+    return LimitDecision(allowed=True, retry_after=None, remaining=remaining, reason=None)
+
+
+def _check_now_valid(now: float) -> float:
+    if not isinstance(now, (int, float)):
+        raise ValueError("now must be a number")
+    now_f = float(now)
+    if not math.isfinite(now_f):
+        raise ValueError("now must be finite")
+    if now_f < 0:
+        raise ValueError("now must be >= 0")
+    return now_f
+
+
+class LimitState:
+    def __init__(self, policy: LimitPolicy) -> None:
+        self.policy = policy
+        self._timestamps: list[float] = []
+        self._total: int = 0
+        self._last: float | None = None
+
+    def check(self, now: float) -> LimitDecision:
+        now_f = _check_now_valid(now)
+        if self._last is not None and now_f < self._last:
+            raise ValueError("time must not go backwards")
+        # compute in-window from stored timestamps
+        if self.policy.rate_limit is not None:
+            per = float(self.policy.rate_limit.per_seconds)
+            in_window = [t for t in self._timestamps if now_f - t < per]
+            in_window_count = len(in_window)
+        else:
+            in_window = None
+            in_window_count = None
+        used = self._total
+
+        rate_denies = False
+        if self.policy.rate_limit is not None:
+            assert in_window_count is not None
+            if in_window_count >= self.policy.rate_limit.max_calls:
+                rate_denies = True
+        quota_denies = False
+        if self.policy.quota is not None:
+            if used >= self.policy.quota.max_calls:
+                quota_denies = True
+
+        if quota_denies:
+            return LimitDecision(allowed=False, retry_after=None, remaining=0, reason="quota")
+        if rate_denies:
+            assert in_window is not None
+            assert in_window_count is not None
+            assert self.policy.rate_limit is not None
+            sorted_w = sorted(in_window)
+            idx = in_window_count - self.policy.rate_limit.max_calls
+            blocking = sorted_w[idx]
+            retry_after = blocking + float(self.policy.rate_limit.per_seconds) - now_f
+            return LimitDecision(
+                allowed=False, retry_after=retry_after, remaining=0, reason="rate_limit"
+            )
+        if self.policy.rate_limit is None and self.policy.quota is None:
+            return LimitDecision(allowed=True, retry_after=None, remaining=None, reason=None)
+        remainings: list[int] = []
+        if self.policy.rate_limit is not None:
+            assert in_window_count is not None
+            remainings.append(self.policy.rate_limit.max_calls - in_window_count - 1)
+        if self.policy.quota is not None:
+            remainings.append(self.policy.quota.max_calls - used - 1)
+        remaining = min(remainings)
+        return LimitDecision(allowed=True, retry_after=None, remaining=remaining, reason=None)
+
+    def record(self, now: float) -> None:
+        now_f = _check_now_valid(now)
+        if self._last is not None and now_f < self._last:
+            raise ValueError("time must not go backwards")
+        self._last = now_f
+        self._total += 1
+        if self.policy.rate_limit is not None:
+            per = float(self.policy.rate_limit.per_seconds)
+            self._timestamps.append(now_f)
+            # drop timestamps outside window relative to recorded now
+            self._timestamps = [t for t in self._timestamps if now_f - t < per]
+        else:
+            # Without a rate limit no timestamps need to be kept at all.
+            pass
+
+    def reset(self) -> None:
+        self._timestamps = []
+        self._total = 0
+        self._last = None

+from typing import Literal, Optional
+import math
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator
+
+class RateLimit(BaseModel):
+    max_calls: int = Field(..., gt=0)
+    per_seconds: float = Field(..., gt=0)
+
+    @field_validator("per_seconds")
+    @classmethod
+    def validate_per_seconds(cls, v: float) -> float:
+        if not math.isfinite(v):
+            raise ValueError("per_seconds must be finite")
+        return v
+
+class Quota(BaseModel):
+    max_calls: int = Field(..., gt=0)
+
+class LimitPolicy(BaseModel):
+    rate_limit: Optional[RateLimit] = None
+    quota: Optional[Quota] = None
+    scope: Literal["server", "session"] = "server"
+
+class LimitDecision(BaseModel):
+    allowed: bool
+    retry_after: Optional[float] = None
+    remaining: Optional[int] = None
+    reason: Optional[Literal["rate_limit", "quota"]] = None
+
+def evaluate(policy: LimitPolicy, call_times: list[float], now: float) -> LimitDecision:
+    if not math.isfinite(now) or now < 0:
+        raise ValueError("now must be finite and >= 0")
+    for t in call_times:
+        if not math.isfinite(t) or t > now:
+            raise ValueError("call times must be finite and <= now")
+
+    if policy.rate_limit is None and policy.quota is None:
+        return LimitDecision(allowed=True, retry_after=None, remaining=None, reason=None)
+
+    quota_denied = False
+    quota_remaining = None
+    if policy.quota is not None:
+        used = len(call_times)
+        if used >= policy.quota.max_calls:
+            quota_denied = True
+        else:
+            quota_remaining = policy.quota.max_calls - used - 1
+
+    rate_denied = False
+    rate_remaining = None
+    retry_after = None
+    if policy.rate_limit is not None:
+        per_sec = policy.rate_limit.per_seconds
+        max_c = policy.rate_limit.max_calls
+        in_window_times = [t for t in call_times if (now - t) < per_sec]
+        in_window_count = len(in_window_times)
+        if in_window_count >= max_c:
+            rate_denied = True
+            in_window_times.sort()
+            oldest_blocking = in_window_times[in_window_count - max_c]
+            retry_after = oldest_blocking + per_sec - now
+            if retry_after < 0:
+                retry_after = 0.0
+        else:
+            rate_remaining = max_c - in_window_count - 1
+
+    if quota_denied:
+        return LimitDecision(allowed=False, retry_after=None, remaining=0, reason="quota")
+    
+    if rate_denied:
+        return LimitDecision(allowed=False, retry_after=retry_after, remaining=0, reason="rate_limit")
+
+    rems = [r for r in [rate_remaining, quota_remaining] if r is not None]
+    rem = min(rems) if rems else None
+    return LimitDecision(allowed=True, retry_after=None, remaining=rem, reason=None)
+
+class LimitState:
+    def __init__(self, policy: LimitPolicy) -> None:
+        self.policy = policy
+        self._timestamps: list[float] = []
+        self._pruned_quota_count: int = 0
+        self._total_quota_count: int = 0
+        self._last_now: Optional[float] = None
+
+    def _validate_now(self, now: float) -> None:
+        if not math.isfinite(now) or now < 0:
+            raise ValueError("now must be finite and >= 0")
+        if self._last_now is not None and now < self._last_now:
+            raise ValueError("Time must not go backwards")
+
+    def check(self, now: float) -> LimitDecision:
+        self._validate_now(now)
+        if self.policy.rate_limit is None and self.policy.quota is None:
+            return LimitDecision(allowed=True, retry_after=None, remaining=None, reason=None)
+        
+        # Determine call_times for evaluate
+        if self.policy.rate_limit is not None:
+            per_sec = self.policy.rate_limit.per_seconds
+            kept = [t for t in self._timestamps if (now - t) < per_sec]
+            pruned = len(self._timestamps) - len(kept)
+            total_used = len(kept) + self._pruned_quota_count + pruned
+            # We need call_times to have length total_used, with kept timestamps in window.
+            # We can put (total_used - len(kept)) dummy timestamps at -1.0 (or now - per_sec - 1.0)
+            dummy_count = total_used - len(kept)
+            call_times = kept + [-1.0] * dummy_count
+            return evaluate(self.policy, call_times, now)
+        else:
+            call_times = [0.0] * self._total_quota_count
+            return evaluate(self.policy, call_times, now)
+
+    def record(self, now: float) -> None:
+        self._validate_now(now)
+        self._last_now = now
+        if self.policy.rate_limit is not None:
+            per_sec = self.policy.rate_limit.per_seconds
+            kept = []
+            pruned = 0
+            for t in self._timestamps:
+                if (now - t) < per_sec:
+                    kept.append(t)
+                else:
+                    pruned += 1
+            self._timestamps = kept
+            self._pruned_quota_count += pruned
+            self._timestamps.append(now)
+        else:
+            self._total_quota_count += 1
+
+    def reset(self) -> None:
+        self._timestamps = []
+        self._pruned_quota_count = 0
+        self._total_quota_count = 0
+        self._last_now = None

+import pytest
+from pydantic import ValidationError
+from mcp.server.mcpserver.limits import (

+    Quota,
+    LimitPolicy,
+    LimitDecision,
+    evaluate,
+    LimitState,
+)
+
+def test_rate_limit_validation():
+    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
+        RateLimit(max_calls=0, per_seconds=10.0)
+    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
+        RateLimit(max_calls=-1, per_seconds=10.0)
+    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
+        RateLimit(max_calls=5, per_seconds=0.0)
+    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
+        RateLimit(max_calls=5, per_seconds=-1.0)
+    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
+        RateLimit(max_calls=5, per_seconds=float("inf"))
+    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
+        RateLimit(max_calls=5, per_seconds=float("nan"))
+
+def test_quota_validation():
+    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
+        Quota(max_calls=0)
+    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
+        Quota(max_calls=-5)
+
+def test_limit_policy_scope():
+    policy = LimitPolicy(scope="server")
+    assert policy.scope == "server"
+    policy2 = LimitPolicy(scope="session")
+    assert policy2.scope == "session"
+    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
+        LimitPolicy(scope="invalid")
+
+def test_evaluate_examples():
+    # RateLimit example
+    rl = RateLimit(max_calls=2, per_seconds=10.0)
+    policy = LimitPolicy(rate_limit=rl)
+    
+    # at now=9.999 denied with retry_after ~= 0.001
+    dec = evaluate(policy, [0.0, 5.0], 9.999)
+    assert dec.allowed is False
+    assert dec.reason == "rate_limit"
+    assert dec.retry_after is not None
+    assert abs(dec.retry_after - 0.001) < 1e-4
+    assert dec.remaining == 0
+
+    # at now=10.0 allowed with remaining=0 (the call at 0.0 has left)
+    dec2 = evaluate(policy, [0.0, 5.0], 10.0)
+    assert dec2.allowed is True
+    assert dec2.remaining == 0
+
+    # Quota example
+    q = Quota(max_calls=3)
+    q_policy = LimitPolicy(quota=q)
+    dec3 = evaluate(q_policy, [1.0, 2.0], 100.0)
+    assert dec3.allowed is True
+    assert dec3.remaining == 0
+
+    dec4 = evaluate(q_policy, [1.0, 2.0, 3.0], 100.0)
+    assert dec4.allowed is False
+    assert dec4.reason == "quota"
+    assert dec4.retry_after is None
+    assert dec4.remaining == 0
+
+def test_limit_state():
+    rl = RateLimit(max_calls=2, per_seconds=10.0)
+    policy = LimitPolicy(rate_limit=rl)
+    state = LimitState(policy)
+
+    state.record(0.0)
+    state.record(5.0)
+
+    # check at 9.999
+    dec = state.check(9.999)
+    assert dec.allowed is False
+    assert dec.reason == "rate_limit"
+
+    # check at 10.0
+    dec2 = state.check(10.0)
+    assert dec2.allowed is True
+
+    state.record(10.0)
+    dec3 = state.check(10.0)
+    assert dec3.allowed is False

+

+

+
+
+class LimitPolicy(BaseModel):
+    """Rate limit and/or quota, applied per server or per session. Empty means unlimited."""
+
+    rate_limit: RateLimit | None = None
+    quota: Quota | None = None
+    scope: Literal["server", "session"] = "server"
+
+
+class LimitDecision(BaseModel):
+    """Outcome of checking whether one more call is allowed."""
+
+    allowed: bool
+    retry_after: float | None = None
+    remaining: int | None = None
+    reason: Literal["rate_limit", "quota"] | None = None
+
+
+def _validate_now(now: float) -> None:
+    if not math.isfinite(now):
+        raise ValueError(f"now must be finite, got {now!r}")
+    if now < 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"now must not be negative, got {now!r}")
+
+
+def _decide(policy: LimitPolicy, window: list[float], used: int, now: float) -> LimitDecision:
+    """Decide given the timestamps still inside the window (any order) and the lifetime call count."""
+    rate = policy.rate_limit
+    quota = policy.quota
+
+    in_window = 0
+    rate_ok = True
+    if rate is not None:
+        window = sorted(t for t in window if now - t < rate.per_seconds)
+        in_window = len(window)
+        rate_ok = in_window < rate.max_calls
+
+    quota_ok = quota is None or used < quota.max_calls
+
+    if not quota_ok:
+        return LimitDecision(allowed=False, retry_after=None, remaining=0, reason="quota")
+
+    if not rate_ok:
+        assert rate is not None
+        blocking = window[in_window - rate.max_calls]
+        retry_after = blocking + rate.per_seconds - now
+        if retry_after <= 0:
+            retry_after = math.nextafter(0.0, 1.0)
+        # Guard against float rounding: at now + retry_after the call must have left the window.
+        for _ in range(8):
+            if (now + retry_after) - blocking >= rate.per_seconds:
+                break
+            retry_after = math.nextafter(retry_after, math.inf)
+        return LimitDecision(allowed=False, retry_after=retry_after, remaining=0, reason="rate_limit")
+
+    remainings: list[int] = []
+    if rate is not None:
+        remainings.append(rate.max_calls - in_window - 1)
+    if quota is not None:
+        remainings.append(quota.max_calls - used - 1)
+    remaining = min(remainings) if remainings else None
+    return LimitDecision(allowed=True, retry_after=None, remaining=remaining, reason=None)
+
+
+def evaluate(policy: LimitPolicy, call_times: list[float], now: float) -> LimitDecision:
+    """Decide whether one more call at `now` is allowed, given earlier allowed call times.
+
+    Does not mutate `call_times`. Raises `ValueError` if `now` is negative or
+    non-finite, or if any entry is non-finite or later than `now`.
+    """
+    _validate_now(now)
+    for t in call_times:
+        if not math.isfinite(t):
+            raise ValueError(f"call time must be finite, got {t!r}")
+        if t > now:
+            raise ValueError(f"call time {t!r} is after now {now!r}")
+    return _decide(policy, list(call_times), len(call_times), now)
+
+
+class LimitState:
+    """In-memory tracker of calls for one policy and one scope."""
+
+    def __init__(self, policy: LimitPolicy) -> None:
+        self.policy = policy
+        self._times: deque[float] = deque()
+        self._count = 0
+        self._last: float | None = None
+
+    def _validate(self, now: float) -> None:
+        _validate_now(now)
+        if self._last is not None and now < self._last:
+            raise ValueError(f"time went backwards: {now!r} is before last recorded call {self._last!r}")
+
+    def check(self, now: float) -> LimitDecision:
+        """Return what `evaluate` would for all recorded calls. Records nothing."""
+        self._validate(now)
+        return _decide(self.policy, list(self._times), self._count, now)
+
+    def record(self, now: float) -> None:
+        """Record one call at `now`, unconditionally."""
+        self._validate(now)
+        self._count += 1
+        self._last = now
+        rate = self.policy.rate_limit
+        if rate is not None:
+            self._times.append(now)
+            while self._times and now - self._times[0] >= rate.per_seconds:
+                self._times.popleft()
+
+    def reset(self) -> None:
+        """Forget all recorded calls."""
+        self._times.clear()
+        self._count = 0
+        self._last = None

+        else:
+            remaining = None
+
+        return LimitDecision(
+            allowed=True,
+            retry_after=None,
+            remaining=remaining,
+            reason=None,

+        self._last_now = now

+import pytest
+from mcp.server.mcpserver.exceptions import ToolError
+from mcp.server.mcpserver.limits import LimitPolicy, Quota, RateLimit
+from mcp.server.mcpserver.tools import Tool, ToolManager
+
+
+def test_tool_limits_field():
+    def sample() -> int:
+        return 42
+
+    policy = LimitPolicy(quota=Quota(max_calls=5))
+    tool = Tool.from_function(sample, limits=policy)
+    assert tool.limits == policy
+
+    tool_none = Tool.from_function(sample)
+    assert tool_none.limits is None
+
+
+def test_tool_manager_add_tool_limits():
+    def sample() -> int:
+        return 42
+
+    policy = LimitPolicy(rate_limit=RateLimit(max_calls=10, per_seconds=60))
+    manager = ToolManager()
+    tool = manager.add_tool(sample, limits=policy)
+    assert tool.limits == policy
+    assert manager.get_limits("sample") == policy
+    assert manager.get_tool("sample").limits == policy
+
+
+def test_tool_manager_duplicate_tool_ignores_new_limits():
+    def sample1() -> int:
+        return 1
+
+    def sample2() -> int:
+        return 2
+
+    policy1 = LimitPolicy(quota=Quota(max_calls=1))
+    policy2 = LimitPolicy(quota=Quota(max_calls=2))
+
+    manager = ToolManager()
+    t1 = manager.add_tool(sample1, name="sample", limits=policy1)
+    assert t1.limits == policy1
+
+    # Duplicate add with same name should return existing tool unchanged, ignoring new limits
+    t2 = manager.add_tool(sample2, name="sample", limits=policy2)
+    assert t2 is t1
+    assert t2.limits == policy1
+    assert manager.get_limits("sample") == policy1
+
+
+def test_tool_manager_init_with_tools_keeps_limits():
+    def sample() -> int:
+        return 42
+
+    policy = LimitPolicy(quota=Quota(max_calls=3))
+    tool = Tool.from_function(sample, limits=policy)
+    manager = ToolManager(tools=[tool])
+    assert manager.get_limits("sample") == policy
+    assert manager.get_tool("sample").limits == policy
+
+
+def test_get_limits_unknown_tool():
+    manager = ToolManager()
+    assert manager.get_limits("unknown") is None
+
+
+def test_set_limits_success_and_removal():
+    def sample() -> int:
+        return 42
+

+import pytest
+
+from mcp.server.mcpserver.resources import FunctionResource, ResourceManager
+from mcp.server.mcpserver.resources.base import content_size
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("content", "expected"),
+    [("abc", 3), ("é", 2), ("漢字", 6), ("🎉", 4), ("", 0), (b"\x00\x01\x02", 3)],
+)
+def test_content_size(content: str | bytes, expected: int) -> None:
+    assert content_size(content) == expected
+
+
+def _resource(uri: str = "test://r") -> FunctionResource:
+    return FunctionResource(uri=uri, name="r", fn=lambda: "x")  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [0, -1])
+def test_add_resource_rejects_non_positive(bad: int) -> None:
+    manager = ResourceManager()
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="max_bytes"):
+        manager.add_resource(_resource(), max_bytes=bad)
+    assert manager.list_resources() == []
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [0, -1])
+def test_add_template_rejects_non_positive(bad: int) -> None:
+    manager = ResourceManager()
+
+    def fn(x: str) -> str:
+        return x  # pragma: no cover
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="max_bytes"):
+        manager.add_template(fn, "docs://{x}", max_bytes=bad)
+    assert manager.list_templates() == []
+
+
+def test_max_bytes_is_keyword_only() -> None:
+    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
+        ResourceManager().add_resource(_resource(), 5)  # type: ignore[misc]
+
+
+def test_max_bytes_for_static_and_template() -> None:
+    manager = ResourceManager()
+    manager.add_resource(_resource("test://a"), max_bytes=5)
+    manager.add_resource(_resource("test://b"))
+
+    def fn(x: str) -> str:
+        return x  # pragma: no cover
+
+    manager.add_template(fn, "docs://{x}", max_bytes=7)
+    assert manager.max_bytes_for("test://a") == 5
+    assert manager.max_bytes_for("test://b") is None
+    assert manager.max_bytes_for("docs://abc") == 7
+    assert manager.max_bytes_for("nope://x") is None
+
+
+def test_duplicate_static_first_cap_wins() -> None:
+    manager = ResourceManager(warn_on_duplicate_resources=False)
+    manager.add_resource(_resource("test://a"), max_bytes=5)
+    manager.add_resource(_resource("test://a"), max_bytes=50)
+    assert manager.max_bytes_for("test://a") == 5

+from typing import Any, cast
+
+import anyio
+import pytest
+
+from mcp.server.mcpserver.exceptions import ToolError, UnexpectedToolError
+from mcp.server.mcpserver.tools import Tool, ToolManager
+
+CTX = cast(Any, None)
+
+
+async def slow() -> str:
+    await anyio.sleep(5)
+    return "done"  # pragma: no cover
+
+
+async def fast() -> str:
+    return "ok"
+
+
+async def raises_timeout() -> str:
+    raise TimeoutError("inner")
+
+
+async def raises_toolerror() -> str:
+    raise ToolError("nope")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [0, -1, 0.0, -0.5])
+def test_non_positive_rejected(bad: float):
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="timeout_seconds"):
+        Tool.from_function(fast, timeout_seconds=bad)
+    manager = ToolManager()
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="timeout_seconds"):
+        manager.add_tool(fast, name="fast", timeout_seconds=bad)
+    assert manager.get_tool("fast") is None
+
+
+def test_small_and_int_accepted():
+    assert Tool.from_function(fast, timeout_seconds=1e-9).timeout_seconds == 1e-9
+    assert Tool.from_function(fast, timeout_seconds=3).timeout_seconds == 3
+    assert Tool.from_function(fast).timeout_seconds is None
+
+
+@pytest.mark.anyio
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("value", "text"),
+    [(0.01, "0.01s"), (0.0123456789, "0.0123457s")],
+)
+async def test_timeout_message(value: float, text: str):
+    manager = ToolManager()
+    manager.add_tool(slow, name="slow", timeout_seconds=value)
+    with pytest.raises(ToolError) as exc:
+        await manager.call_tool("slow", {}, CTX)
+    assert str(exc.value) == f"Tool 'slow' timed out after {text}"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.anyio
+async def test_within_budget_and_isolation():
+    manager = ToolManager()
+    manager.add_tool(fast, name="fast", timeout_seconds=1)
+    manager.add_tool(slow, name="slow", timeout_seconds=0.01)
+    assert await manager.call_tool("fast", {}, CTX) == "ok"
+    with pytest.raises(ToolError, match="timed out"):
+        await manager.call_tool("slow", {}, CTX)
+    assert await manager.call_tool("fast", {}, CTX) == "ok"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.anyio
+async def test_inner_timeout_error_is_crash():
+    manager = ToolManager()
+    manager.add_tool(raises_timeout, name="t", timeout_seconds=5)
+    with pytest.raises(UnexpectedToolError) as exc:
+        await manager.call_tool("t", {}, CTX)
+    assert "timed out" not in str(exc.value)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.anyio
+async def test_other_failures_unchanged():
+    manager = ToolManager()
+    manager.add_tool(raises_toolerror, name="r", timeout_seconds=5)
+    with pytest.raises(ToolError, match="Error executing tool r: nope"):
+        await manager.call_tool("r", {}, CTX)
+    with pytest.raises(ToolError, match="Unknown tool: zzz"):
+        await manager.call_tool("zzz", {}, CTX)

+import pytest
+
+from mcp.server.mcpserver.resources import FunctionResource, ResourceManager
+from mcp.server.mcpserver.resources.base import content_size
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("content", "expected"),
+    [("abc", 3), ("é", 2), ("漢字", 6), ("🎉", 4), ("", 0), (b"\x00\x01\x02", 3), (b"", 0)],
+)
+def test_content_size(content: str | bytes, expected: int):
+    assert content_size(content) == expected
+
+
+def _resource(uri: str = "test://r") -> FunctionResource:
+    return FunctionResource(uri=uri, name="r", fn=lambda: "x")  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [0, -1])
+def test_manager_add_resource_rejects_non_positive(bad: int):
+    manager = ResourceManager()
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="max_bytes"):
+        manager.add_resource(_resource(), max_bytes=bad)
+    assert manager.list_resources() == []
+
+
+def test_manager_add_resource_max_bytes_is_keyword_only():
+    manager = ResourceManager()
+    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
+        manager.add_resource(_resource(), 5)  # type: ignore[misc]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [0, -1])
+def test_manager_add_template_rejects_non_positive(bad: int):
+    manager = ResourceManager()
+
+    def fn(x: str) -> str:
+        return x  # pragma: no cover
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="max_bytes"):
+        manager.add_template(fn, "docs://{x}", max_bytes=bad)
+    assert manager.list_templates() == []
+
+
+def test_manager_get_max_bytes():
+    manager = ResourceManager()
+    manager.add_resource(_resource("test://capped"), max_bytes=5)
+    manager.add_resource(_resource("test://free"))
+
+    def fn(x: str) -> str:
+        return x  # pragma: no cover
+
+    manager.add_template(fn, "docs://{x}", max_bytes=3)
+    assert manager.get_max_bytes("test://capped") == 5
+    assert manager.get_max_bytes("test://free") is None
+    assert manager.get_max_bytes("docs://abc") == 3
+    assert manager.get_max_bytes("other://abc") is None
+
+
+def test_manager_duplicate_keeps_first_cap():
+    manager = ResourceManager(warn_on_duplicate_resources=False)
+    manager.add_resource(_resource("test://r"), max_bytes=5)
+    manager.add_resource(_resource("test://r"), max_bytes=100)
+    assert manager.get_max_bytes("test://r") == 5

+import pytest
+from mcp_types import CallToolResult, TextContent
+
+from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer
+from mcp.server.mcpserver.exceptions import ToolError
+from mcp.server.mcpserver.tools.base import Tool, deprecation_message
+from mcp.server.mcpserver.tools.tool_manager import ToolManager
+
+
+def test_deprecation_message():
+    assert deprecation_message("a", False) is None
+    assert deprecation_message("a", True) == "Tool 'a' is deprecated"
+    assert deprecation_message("get-v1", "get v2") == "Tool 'get-v1' is deprecated; use 'get v2' instead"
+    for bad in ("", "  "):
+        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="deprecated"):
+            deprecation_message("a", bad)
+
+
+def test_empty_rejected_everywhere():
+    def f() -> str:
+        return "x"
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="deprecated"):
+        Tool.from_function(f, deprecated=" ")
+    manager = ToolManager()
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="deprecated"):
+        manager.add_tool(f, deprecated="")
+    assert manager.list_tools() == []
+    server = MCPServer("s")
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="deprecated"):
+        server.add_tool(f, deprecated="")
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="deprecated"):
+        server.tool(deprecated="  ")(f)
+    assert server._tool_manager.list_tools() == []  # pyright: ignore[reportPrivateUsage]
+
+
+async def test_list_and_call():
+    server = MCPServer("s")
+    own = {"k": 1, "deprecated": False}
+
+    @server.tool(deprecated="new", meta=own)
+    def old() -> str:
+        return "hi"
+
+    @server.tool(deprecated=True)
+    def old2() -> str:
+        return "hi"
+
+    @server.tool()
+    def fresh() -> str:
+        return "hi"
+
+    @server.tool(deprecated=True)
+    def boom() -> str:
+        raise ToolError("bad input")
+
+    @server.tool(deprecated=True)
+    def own_result() -> CallToolResult:
+        return CallToolResult(content=[TextContent(type="text", text="x")], _meta={"a": 1})
+
+    tools = {t.name: t for t in await server.list_tools()}
+    assert tools["old"].meta == {"k": 1, "deprecated": True, "replacement": "new"}
+    assert own == {"k": 1, "deprecated": False}
+    assert tools["old2"].meta == {"deprecated": True, "replacement": None}
+    assert tools["fresh"].meta is None
+

+            if stored_policy == policy:

+    def decide(

+    def record(

+        scope_key: str | None,

+
+    def __call__(self) -> float:
+        return self.t
+
+

+    clock = FakeClock()
+    enforcer = LimitEnforcer(clock=clock)

+    assert enforcer.remaining("t", policy, None) == 2

+    assert enforcer.remaining("t", policy, None) == 3

+
+

+    server = MCPServer("test")
+    server._tool_manager.enforcer = LimitEnforcer(clock=FakeClock())

+    def search() -> str:
+        return "ok"
+
+    async with Client(server) as client:
+        first = await client.call_tool("search", {})
+        assert not first.is_error
+        second = await client.call_tool("search", {})
+        assert second.is_error
+        content = second.content[0]
+        assert isinstance(content, TextContent)
+        assert content.text == "Tool 'search' quota exhausted"
+

+_StateKey = str | tuple[str, str]
+
+
+class LimitEnforcer:
+    """Tracks per-tool (and per-session) call history and enforces LimitPolicy."""
+
+    def __init__(self, clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic) -> None:
+        self._clock = clock
+        self._states: dict[_StateKey, LimitState] = {}
+
+    def _now(self, now: float | None) -> float:
+        return self._clock() if now is None else now
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _key(tool_name: str, policy: LimitPolicy, scope_key: str | None) -> _StateKey:
+        if policy.scope == "session" and scope_key is not None:
+            return (tool_name, scope_key)
+        return tool_name
+
+    def _state(self, tool_name: str, policy: LimitPolicy, scope_key: str | None) -> LimitState:
+        key = self._key(tool_name, policy, scope_key)
+        state = self._states.get(key)
+        if state is None or state.policy != policy:
+            state = LimitState(policy)
+            self._states[key] = state
+        return state
+
+    def decide(
+        self, tool_name: str, policy: LimitPolicy, scope_key: str | None, now: float | None = None
+    ) -> LimitDecision:
+        state = self._state(tool_name, policy, scope_key)
+        return state.check(self._now(now))
+
+    def record(self, tool_name: str, policy: LimitPolicy, scope_key: str | None, now: float | None = None) -> None:
+        state = self._state(tool_name, policy, scope_key)
+        state.record(self._now(now))
+
+    def remaining(
+        self, tool_name: str, policy: LimitPolicy, scope_key: str | None, now: float | None = None
+    ) -> int | None:
+        if policy.rate_limit is None and policy.quota is None:
+            return None
+        decision = self.decide(tool_name, policy, scope_key, now)
+        if not decision.allowed:
+            return 0
+        assert decision.remaining is not None
+        return decision.remaining + 1
+
+    def reset(self, tool_name: str | None = None) -> None:
+        if tool_name is None:
+            self._states.clear()
+            return
+        for key in list(self._states):
+            if key == tool_name or (isinstance(key, tuple) and key[0] == tool_name):
+                del self._states[key]

+def _patch(seg: str) -> str:
+    seg, n1 = re.subn(
+        r"(        structured_output: bool \| None = None,\n)(    \))",
+        r"\1        *,\n        limits: LimitPolicy | None = None,\n\2",
+        seg,
+        count=1,
+    )
+    seg, n2 = re.subn(
+        r"(\n( +)- If False, unconditionally creates an unstructured tool\n)",
+        r"\1\2limits: Optional LimitPolicy enforced when the tool is called (rate limit and/or quota)\n"
+        if False
+        else r"\1",
+        seg,
+        count=1,
+    )
+    m = re.search(r"\n( +)- If False, unconditionally creates an unstructured tool\n", seg)
+    assert m is not None
+    indent = m.group(1)[:-4]
+    seg = (
+        seg[: m.end()]
+        + f"{indent}limits: Optional LimitPolicy enforced when the tool is called (rate limit and/or quota)\n"
+        + seg[m.end() :]
+    )
+    seg, n3 = re.subn(
+        r"( +)structured_output=structured_output,\n",
+        r"\1structured_output=structured_output,\n\1limits=limits,\n",
+        seg,
+        count=1,
+    )
+    assert n1 == 1 and n3 == 1, (n1, n2, n3)
+    return seg
+
+

+import pytest
+
+from mcp.server.mcpserver import Context, MCPServer
+from mcp.server.mcpserver.limits import LimitPolicy, RateLimit
+
+
+def _tool_meta(tools, name):
+    return next(t for t in tools if t.name == name).meta
+
+
+@pytest.mark.anyio
+async def test_unlimited_tool_meta_unchanged():
+    server = MCPServer("t")
+
+    @server.tool()
+    def plain() -> str:
+        return "x"
+
+    tools = await server.list_tools()
+    assert _tool_meta(tools, "plain") is None
+
+
+@pytest.mark.anyio
+async def test_limits_published_and_idempotent():
+    server = MCPServer("t")
+
+    @server.tool(limits=LimitPolicy(rate_limit=RateLimit(max_calls=5, per_seconds=60)), meta={"a": 1, "limits": "x"})
+    def limited() -> str:
+        return "x"
+
+    expected = {
+        "a": 1,
+        "limits": {"rate_limit": {"max_calls": 5, "per_seconds": 60.0}, "quota": None, "scope": "server"},
+    }
+    assert _tool_meta(await server.list_tools(), "limited") == expected
+    assert _tool_meta(await server.list_tools(), "limited") == expected
+
+
+def test_context_without_server_raises():
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="outside of a request"):
+        Context().tool_limits("x")
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="outside of a request"):
+        Context().remaining_calls("x")

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import pytest
+from mcp.server.mcpserver.limits import LimitEnforcer, LimitPolicy, Quota
+from mcp.server.mcpserver.server import MCPServer
+from mcp.client import Client
+
+
+def test_limit_enforcer_forget_scope():
+    enforcer = LimitEnforcer()
+    policy = LimitPolicy(quota=Quota(max_calls=2), scope="session")
+    
+    # Decide & record for session A
+    assert enforcer.decide("tool1", policy, "sessionA").allowed
+    enforcer.record("tool1", policy, "sessionA")
+    assert not enforcer.decide("tool1", policy, "sessionA").allowed
+
+    # Session B should still be allowed
+    assert enforcer.decide("tool1", policy, "sessionB").allowed
+
+    # Forget session A
+    enforcer.forget_scope("sessionA")
+
+    # Session A should now be fresh
+    assert enforcer.decide("tool1", policy, "sessionA").allowed
+    # Unknown scope_key is a no-op
+    enforcer.forget_scope("unknown")
+
+
+def test_mcpserver_forget_session_limits():
+    server = MCPServer()
+    @server.add_tool(limits=LimitPolicy(quota=Quota(max_calls=1), scope="session"))
+    def my_tool() -> str:
+        return "ok"
+
+    server.forget_session_limits("sess1")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.anyio
+async def test_session_scope_clients_isolated():
+    server = MCPServer()
+    
+    @server.add_tool(limits=LimitPolicy(quota=Quota(max_calls=1), scope="session"))
+    def limited_tool() -> str:
+        return "ok"
+
+    async with server.run_in_memory(mode="legacy") as client1, server.run_in_memory(mode="legacy") as client2:
+        # Call limited_tool on client1
+        res1 = await client1.call_tool("limited_tool", {})
+        assert res1
+
+        # Second call on client1 should exhaust quota
+        with pytest.raises(Exception):
+            await client1.call_tool("limited_tool", {})
+
+        # client2 should still have full budget
+        res2 = await client2.call_tool("limited_tool", {})
+        assert res2

+from __future__ import annotations

+import pytest

+from mcp.server.mcpserver.server import MCPServer
+

+def test_limit_enforcer_forget_scope() -> None:
+    enforcer = LimitEnforcer()
+    policy = LimitPolicy(quota=Quota(max_calls=1), scope="session")
+    enforcer.record("tool1", policy, "session_A")
+    enforcer.record("tool1", policy, "session_B")
+    
+    assert not enforcer.decide("tool1", policy, "session_A").allowed
+    assert not enforcer.decide("tool1", policy, "session_B").allowed
+    
+    enforcer.forget_scope("session_A")
+    assert enforcer.decide("tool1", policy, "session_A").allowed
+    assert not enforcer.decide("tool1", policy, "session_B").allowed
+
+
+def test_mcpserver_forget_session_limits() -> None:
+    server = MCPServer("test")
+    @server._tool_manager.add_tool(limits=LimitPolicy(quota=Quota(max_calls=1), scope="session"))
+    def my_tool() -> str:
+        return "ok"
+    
+    enforcer = server._tool_manager.enforcer
+    policy = server._tool_manager.get_limits("my_tool")
+    enforcer.record("my_tool", policy, "session_X")
+    assert not enforcer.decide("my_tool", policy, "session_X").allowed
+    
+    server.forget_session_limits("session_X")
+    assert enforcer.decide("my_tool", policy, "session_X").allowed
